findings.title: forEach with async callback discards promises; try/catch is ineffective
findings.body: Using `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` does not await the async callbacks. The returned promises are discarded, so: (1) the surrounding try/catch on line 124 will never catch errors thrown inside the callback, and (2) the function may return `true` (line 151) before calendar/video deletions have actually completed. This should be replaced with `for...of` or `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` to properly await and catch errors.

findings.title: forEach with async callback discards promises; try/catch is ineffective
findings.body: Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` fires async callbacks without awaiting them. The try/catch on line 124 cannot catch rejections from the async callbacks, and the function proceeds to send emails before deletions complete.

findings.title: forEach with async callback causes race condition between deletion and email
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` starts async calendar/video deletion operations but does not await them. The code immediately proceeds to `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` on line 570 without waiting for the deletions to finish. This means the reschedule email can be sent while calendar events are still being deleted, and any errors from deletion are silently lost as unhandled promise rejections.

findings.title: forEach with async callback means apiDeletes may be empty when Promise.all is called
findings.body: On lines 458-470, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` pushes results into `apiDeletes` inside async callbacks that are not awaited. By the time `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` is reached on line 652, the forEach callbacks may not have executed yet, so `apiDeletes` could be empty or incomplete. Calendar events for recurring bookings may never actually be deleted. Replace with a `for...of` loop or collect promises with `map`.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials implicitly returns Promise in calendar field without being async
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` is a synchronous function that calls `getCalendar(credential)` which now returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`. The returned array elements have `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `calendar: Calendar | null`. While `getConnectedCalendars` correctly awaits `item.calendar`, any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that expects a resolved Calendar will receive a Promise. The function's return type has silently changed, which is a contract break for external callers.

findings.title: Sequential awaits in getVideoAdapters loop instead of parallel
findings.body: The `for...of` loop with `await appStore[appName]` on line 26 processes each credential sequentially. Since each dynamic import is independent, using `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...))` would resolve them in parallel, reducing latency when multiple video credentials are present.
